52465-the-faithful-servant-a-sermon-prea.title: The Faithful Servant A Sermon Preached In St Peter S Southbo
52465-the-faithful-servant-a-sermon-prea.creator: God.
52465-the-faithful-servant-a-sermon-prea.description: A book by God.. It does not say, “Thou hast been rich,” or “great,” or “powerful,” or “brilliant,” but “faithful.”  And it is remarkable that the master said exactly the same words to the servant who had the two talents, as he did to the one that had the five. They were not equally gifted, but both were declared to be faithful. This is a great encouragement for those who are conscious that they have not the same gifts as our venerable father.

arxiv-2105-11439.title: 2nd-order Updates with 1st-order Complexity
arxiv-2105-11439.creator: Michael F. Zimmer
arxiv-2105-11439.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Michael F. Zimmer. It has long been a goal to efficiently compute and use second order information on a function ( f f ) to assist in numerical approximations. Here it is shown how, using only basic physics and a numerical approximation, such information can be accurately obtained at a cost of 𝒪 ⁡ ( N ) {\cal O}(N) complexity, where N N is the dimensionality of the parameter space of f f .

arxiv-2206-03313.title: Quantum oblivious transfer: a short review
arxiv-2206-03313.creator: Manuel B. Santos 1,2 , Paulo Mateus 1,2 , Armando N. Pinto 3,4
arxiv-2206-03313.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Manuel B. Santos 1,2 , Paulo Mateus 1,2 , Armando N. Pinto 3,4. Quantum cryptography is the field of cryptography that explores the quantum properties of matter. Generally, it aims to develop primitives beyond the reach of classical cryptography and to improve existing classical implementations. Although much of the work in this field covers quantum key distribution (QKD), there have been some crucial steps towards the understanding and development of quantum oblivious transfer (QOT).

arxiv-2208-09933.title: AA-Forecast: Anomaly-Aware Forecast for Extreme Events
arxiv-2208-09933.creator: Ashkan Farhangi, Jiang Bian, Arthur Huang, Haoyi Xiong, Jun Wang, Zhishan Guo
arxiv-2208-09933.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ashkan Farhangi, Jiang Bian, Arthur Huang, Haoyi Xiong, Jun Wang, Zhishan Guo. Time series models often deal with extreme events and anomalies, both prevalent in real-world datasets. Such models often need to provide careful probabilistic forecasting, which is vital in risk management for extreme events such as hurricanes and pandemics. However, it is challenging to automatically detect and learn to use extreme events and anomalies for large-scale datasets, which often require manual effort.

arxiv-2209-03857.title: Goos-Hänchen lateral displacements and angular deviations: When these optical effects offset each other Journal: Photonics 9 , 643-14 ( 2022) .
arxiv-2209-03857.creator: \names Stefano De Leo 1,3 , Luca Maggio 2 , Moreno d’Ambrosio 2
arxiv-2209-03857.description: Abstract \logo \mathbf{\Sigma\hskip 1.70709pt\delta\hskip 1.13791pt\Lambda} \titlelines 3 \imgbgabstract For optical beams, transmitted by a right angle prism, the Goos-Hänchen shift can never be seen as a pure effect. Indeed, the lateral displacement, caused by the total internal reflection, will always be accompanied by angular deviations generated by the transmission through the incoming and outgoing interfaces.

Static information flow control (IFC) systems provide the ability to restrict data flows within a program, enabling vulnerable functionality or confidential data to be statically isolated from unsecured data or program logic.

arxiv-2304-08966.title: Predicting the Charge Density Response in Metal Electrodes
arxiv-2304-08966.creator: Andrea Grisafi, Augustin Bussy, Mathieu Salanne, Rodolphe Vuilleumier
arxiv-2304-08966.description: Abstract The computational study of energy storage and conversion processes calls for simulation techniques that can reproduce the electronic response of metal electrodes under electric fields. Despite recent advancements in machine-learning methods applied to electronic-structure properties, predicting the non-local behavior of the charge density in electronic conductors remains a major open challenge.

arxiv-2401-17278.title: Characterising X-ray variability in light curves with complex sampling patterns: application to the eROSITA south ecliptic pole survey
arxiv-2401-17278.creator: D. Bogensberger, K. Nandra, J. Buchner
arxiv-2401-17278.description: Abstract Aims : During its all-sky survey phase, the eROSITA X-ray telescope onboard SRG scans through the ecliptic poles every 4 hours. This extensive data set of long-duration, frequent, and consistent observations of thousands of X-ray sources is ideal for a detailed long-term X-ray variability analysis.

arxiv-2403-16590.title: Extremal properties of max-autoregressive moving average processes for modelling extreme river flows
arxiv-2403-16590.creator: Eleanor D’Arcy, Jonathan A. Tawn
arxiv-2403-16590.description: Abstract Max-autogressive moving average (Max-ARMA) processes are powerful tools for modelling time series data with heavy-tailed behaviour; these are a non-linear version of the popular autoregressive moving average models. River flow data typically have features of heavy tails and non-linearity, as large precipitation events cause sudden spikes in the data that then exponentially decay.

arxiv-2510-04448.title: Quantum Cryptography and Hardness of Non-Collapsing Measurements
arxiv-2510-04448.creator: Tomoyuki Morimae, Yuki Shirakawa, Takashi Yamakawa
arxiv-2510-04448.description: Abstract One-way puzzles (OWPuzzs) introduced by Khurana and Tomer [STOC 2024] are a natural quantum analogue of one-way functions (OWFs), and one of the most fundamental primitives in “Microcrypt” where OWFs do not exist but quantum cryptography is possible. OWPuzzs are implied by almost all quantum cryptographic primitives, and imply several important applications such as non-interactive commitments and multi-party computations.

arxiv-2510-09663.title: Adversarial-Resilient RF Fingerprinting: A CNN-GAN Framework for Rogue Transmitter Detection
arxiv-2510-09663.creator: Raju Dhakal, Prashant Shekhar, Laxima Niure Kandel
arxiv-2510-09663.description: Abstract Radio Frequency Fingerprinting (RFF) has evolved as an effective solution for authenticating devices by leveraging the unique imperfections in hardware components involved in the signal generation process. In this work, we propose a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based framework for detecting rogue devices and identifying genuine ones using softmax probability thresholding.

arxiv-2601-20511.title: Say Cheese! Detail-Preserving Portrait Collection Generation via Natural Language Edits
arxiv-2601-20511.creator: Zelong Sun, Jiahui Wu, Ying Ba, Dong Jing, Zhiwu Lu
arxiv-2601-20511.description: Abstract As social media platforms proliferate, users increasingly demand intuitive ways to create diverse, high-quality portrait collections. In this work, we introduce Portrait Collection Generation (PCG), a novel task that generates coherent portrait collections by editing a reference portrait image through natural language instructions.

pmc-10531904.title: The Combination of Glucocorticoids and Hyaluronic Acid Enhances Efficacy in IL-1β/IL-17-Treated Bovine Osteochondral Grafts Compared with Individual Application
pmc-10531904.creator: Christoph Bauer, Lukas B Moser, Daniela Kern, Vivek Jeyakumar, Stefan Nehrer, Antonella Fioravanti
pmc-10531904.description: Patients with knee osteoarthritis often receive glucocorticoid (GC) or hyaluronic acid (HA) injections to alleviate symptoms. This study evaluated the impact of Triamcinolone Hexacetonide (a GC), HA, and a combination of both on bovine osteochondral grafts exposed to IL-1β and IL-17 in an ex vivo culture. Metabolic activity increased with GC treatment.

pmc-11395260.title: Autologous hGMSC-Derived iPS: A New Proposal for Tissue Regeneration
pmc-11395260.creator: Ylenia Della Rocca, Francesca Diomede, Fanì Konstantinidou, Valentina Gatta, Liborio Stuppia, Umberto Benedetto, Marco Zimarino, Paola Lanuti, Oriana Trubiani, Jacopo Pizzicannella
pmc-11395260.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The high mortality in the global population due to chronic diseases highlights the urgency to identify effective alternative therapies. Regenerative medicine provides promising new approaches for this purpose, particularly in the use of induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). The aim of the work is to establish a new pluripotency cell line obtained for the first time by reprogramming human gingival mesenchymal stem cells (hGMSCs) by a non-integrating method.

De novo variants in snRNA genes RNU4-2 (ReNU syndrome), RNU5B-1 and RNU2-2 have been linked to dominant neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), revealing a large unexpected contribution of noncoding RNA genes to genetic diseases.

pmc-13475504.description: Adverse outcome pathways (AOPs) describe toxicity across levels of biological organization by measurable key events (KEs), thus providing a structured framework for predicting population-level effects. pmc-13476192.title: Descending Necrotizing Mediastinitis Across Age and Host-Status Groups: Diagnosis, Treatment Phases, and Outcomes in the Literature, with an Illustrative Case
pmc-13476192.creator: Constantin Ionescu, Claudia Simona Cambrea, Ionuţ Bulbuc, Elena Neagu, Bogdan Marian Caraban
pmc-13476192.description: IntroductionDescending necrotizing mediastinitis (DNM) is a rare but life-threatening infection originating from odontogenic, tonsillopharyngeal, or deep cervical sources, and propagating through the cervical fascial planes into the mediastinum. Despite advances in cross-sectional imaging, thoracic surgery, intensive care medicine, and antimicrobial therapy, DNM remains associated with mortality ranging from 11 to 40% across contemporary series.

pmc-13513756.creator: Lazar Velicki, Aleksandra Milovancev, Andrej Preveden, Jelena Vuckovic, Miodrag Belopavlovic, Milan Rodic, Nenad Filipovic, Djordje Jakovljevic
pmc-13513756.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is entering cardiac surgery through predictive modelling, multimodal imaging, perioperative monitoring, workflow automation, and emerging computer-vision applications. The most mature evidence concerns risk prediction before and after surgery. Even in this domain, however, systematic reviews show that improvements over conventional statistical models are often modest and that routine clinical implementation remains limited.

uslaw-usc-t43-s641c.title: 43 U.S.C. § 641c — Requirements of application for quitclaim deed
uslaw-usc-t43-s641c.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t43-s641c.description: United States Code, Title 43 (Public Lands); Chapter 14 (Grants Of Desert Lands To States For Reclamation). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The application must include a list of all the lands which the State certifies should be transferred under the terms of section 641a of this title, the basis for the certification of each tract included, and a quitclaim or relinquishment.
